author: Hussain Nasser
headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
Saudi savers now keep more in time and savings deposits than in current accounts. Argaam reports it's the first time since 2008. The slides show why banks care.

End of September, from SAMA data:
Time and savings: SAR 1.417tn, 46.1% of deposits
Demand: SAR 1.405tn, 45.7%
A year earlier the split was 39.3% and 50.4%.

Two things I'd watch:

1. Time deposits pay interest. Current accounts mostly don't. So the same deposit base costs banks more to fund.

2. How much of that reaches margins. Asharq Al-Awsat notes a higher share doesn't have to lift funding costs one for one. Q4 results will show it.

If you work in a bank treasury here, are you seeing it in your cost of funds?

Sources: SAMA data via Asharq Al-Awsat and Argaam

text:
Mubadala and Centerbridge are paying about £1.17bn for Canaccord's UK wealth business. It looks after £43.4bn of client money.

So the price is roughly 2.7% of client assets.

What the buyers have to believe:

1. The money stays. A wealth manager earns a fee on the assets it looks after, so the price only works if clients don't leave.

2. The fees keep growing. Revenue was a reported £261.1m in the year to March 2026, up 11.6%. At £1.17bn, that's about 4.5 times revenue.

Management keeps a meaningful stake, so the people who hold the client relationships stay owners too.

The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

Deal people here: how would you price a wealth manager, on assets or on revenue?

Sources: Mubadala (16 Nov 2026); The National; Family Wealth Report

author: Hussain Nasser
headline: Venture building × AI × games in Saudi Arabia | PE & M&A modelling and valuation | Portfolio Manager, Revival Lab | Investment Director, Glo
text:
Isomorphic Labs has raised $5bn. It still has no drug in clinical trials.

The AI drug discovery company raised $2.1bn in May. Six months later, $5bn more. That's $7.1bn in one year, at a valuation reported at about $50bn.

Two things:

1. Investors are paying for the platform before any human data. The new money is meant to take its first programmes into trials.

2. Gulf capital is in it. Abu Dhabi's MGX came back for this round. Greenoaks and Sequoia co-led.

For GCC life-science funds, it's the same question at a smaller size: how much do you pay for a platform before the first patient?

What would you need to see before backing an AI drug company with no clinical data yet?

Sources: TechCrunch; pharmaphorum (17 Nov 2026)
